title: Boulevard of Bhutan Dreams
contentText:
“Cancel my flight tickets bro”, Vinay said when we were on the way to the Truffles, Residency Road
“Why”, I asked
“I’m going to native on some personal work which can’t be skipped. I’m sorry”, he replied Well, it was initially five of us who had planned to Bhutan. Lately, it was just me, Sachin and Amith who made it. “Hey, where the hell are you?”, I yelled at Sachin over the phone call.
“Will be there in another five.”, He said and cut the call I knew it would be more than half an hour more for him to reach the airport. I and Amith sat over to have a cup of coffee. It was 28th October, roughly having 28 degrees temperature we left from Bengaluru catching our flights to Siliguri. Wondering why did we take up flights to Siliguri rather than Thimpu (capital of Bhutan)?
We had a biking itinerary planned and had to hire bikes from there. Siliguri, a mid developed city in West Bengal which is close to India’s border with Bhutan and Nepal. Personally, nothing much to visit there except a few shopping malls and National wildlife sanctuary. We had reached Siliguri around 2:30 PM, quickly making our way to destination adventures. Santanu Banerjee, proprietor of destination adventures (bike rental company) was there on time and handed over the bike keys after we signed few contract papers and making the payment. We left to Jaigaon as soon as we were done since we had a packed schedule for the rest 8 days. Jaigaon is India’s border with Bhutan. It was a rough journey for us as we left Siliguri around 5 PM and had to ride for 164 km. The sky dusted a bit earlier that day seeming like an 8 o’clock when it was 6 o’clock. It was almost 11 PM when we reached Siliguri having dinner at Hasimara with no other pit stops. The ride was challenging as the temperature lowered to the single digit on the sides of Eastern. Also, we had to adjust ourselves for the newly rented bikes. Jaigaon to Thimpu The huge frame of entrance welcomed us to Bhutan, making the contrast difference of culture and discipline between both the countries. “Hey, park your vehicle right inside the lane.”, The policemen warned when I was just about to park.
“Thanks, officer. I was about to do it the same way.”, I replied calmly
“Sorry man, few Indians just break out of the rules and you seem to be a nicer person”, he left saying so. Well, don’t you want to know why did he make such an intolerant statement? The policemen here will always keep an eye on Indian tourists so that they do not behave the way we behave here like skipping signals, not following rules of the traffic, etc. It was really humiliating but yes, we had to accept it. Also, the border of Jaigaon is full of Kachha roads, giving rise to huge dust when a heavy vehicle just passes by. This misinterpretation made Bhutanese Police think we Indians are all the same. The permit process was bit tiring, we simply hired a broker who would get us permits by charging their fee of 500/- which is really reasonable than you ending up in long queues. It took them almost 6 hours to get us permits and to make additional permit from RTO to our bikes. Vehicle permit ain’t no costlier than 100/- per day. We quickly left after that. It was almost 6 by then and the very next place to reach was Thimpu which was around 170 km. Oh, boys, no highways only ghats. Max to the max you find a 300mts straight road. Imagine the journey time Also, we had a company. Sudheer from Bengaluru was on his solo trip started from Bengaluru covering Nepal and ending up in Bhutan with us. He was a very jovial and like-minded person, so we got along together easily. Roads were well maintained except in few places where it would either be under renovation or would hit by boulders due to the landslides. Entire Bhutan is surrounded by mountains. Few, very few places to visit. We started our journey towards Thimpu by getting stamped on our permit papers. We slowed down our vehicles hearing the honking sound of Amith’s vehicle. (You’re supposed to honk in highways, but not too much) “Not able to ride boys, I will put some towel on my seat and ride, let’s stop for ten minutes”, he said and took out his tower to put on his seat of Royal Enfield. We resumed our journey after the small break and continuously rode for more than 3.5 hours straight without any breaks. Finally, we decided to halt at one hotel for supper which we found with no option. “How far is Thimpu”, I asked the lady who served the hot water
“Ah, 90 km approx, another three hours journey.”, she said Wtf!!!! We rode for four hours almost and just covered 80 km? Yes, it was so worse that we had ended up riding a minimum of 6–7 hours. It was 9 degrees when we started again and not able to ride due to extreme cold. Somehow we managed to reach Thimpu around 12:45 AM and halted in the room which we had booked in prior. How boring it could be, to end up ripping our asses rather than having an adventurous experience. Thimpu We had gotten up after having a good sleep with a complimentary breakfast served over the hotel. It was nothing else than the bread, butter & Jam. The worst part of Bhutan’s entry permit is you only get permission to visit two places; Thimpu and Paro. There are a couple more places which you can cover them but most tourist packages don’t do it. For the other places, we have to obtain permits from the immigration office at Thimpu. Oh yeah, one more day to waste. Since we had made a good plan, we decided to submit all the documents in the immigration office for the permission letter and move on to the sightseeing than waiting there. We duly filled all the forms and submitted while we four including Sudheer had left toMemorial Chorten. Chorten means stupa. The Memorial Chorten, in the heart of the city, is designed in a Tibetan style. Also called the Jangchup Chorten, patterned on the design of a classical stupa, with a pyramidal pillar crowned by a crescent moon and sun. I personally, did not want to visit as I had seen plenty of these in Leh, Kashmir. While I stood at the gate, other boys took a few pictures and came back. We hired a taxi from there and left to Buddha Point. Buddha Pointis situated at some hill having a medium altitude giving enough pleasure for the visitors to have a beautiful sight of Thimpu. There is a giant Buddha statue and a viewpoint exactly straight to it. The Buddha statue is surrounded by a few more smaller statues which were of some Gurus and other eminent Buddhists. “Bro, take some stunning pictures of mine”, I asked Sachin as he took out his DSLR
“You look like a homeless drug addict”, was the comeback given by him for my long hair and beard which I had left it uncut for more than 4 months.
“Not less than a mobster”, Amith hi-fived with Sachin.. Buddha point was the best place in Thimpu We all took some pictures and made our way back to the immigration office to collect the papers. It was done by then, and we immediately rushed to RTO to obtain permits for the bikes. Luckily, we could get it done within a few minutes. Officials, are very polite and helping unless you don’t take them for granted and show your arrogance attitude. Later, in the evening we walked across the local streets and attending the small music festival held in the city center of Thimpu. Bhutanese are having a different dress culture. The men out there wear short gown kind of cloth called Gho and the women wear a small coat type of tops and Dhoti kind bottoms called Kira. Surprising Or Funny? Yes, that’s their culture. Thimpu Punakha Paro “What, where is my coffee?”, I asked seeing the missed cup which I had placed on the table just before I left to brush my teeth.
“It was the worse coffee I ever had”, Sachin said turning from one side to another inside his blanket. We started our journey to Punakha around 8 AM in the morning. It was around 90 km which would make it a four-hour journey. Weather was very cold despite the sun rays. Almost after an hour journey, we reached Dochu La Pass, There is a commemorative site of 108 Chortens (Druk Wangyel) in memory of the Bhutanese soldiers who died whilst fighting Indian rebels in 2003. These are set out in a circular type pattern with a larger Chorten in the center and at the highest peak. Paths and steps criss-cross and encircle the site, allowing great access. Since it was extremely cold, we rushed inside the cafe opposite to it. The ride was full of scenic. We also had a break from our biking journey on the previous day since we roamed around Thimpu in taxis. We had quite of more energy in driving our bikes that day. Almost after 4 hours of straight journey, we ended up inPunakha Dzong. Dzong means the place of happiness. Punakha Dzong was one of the best dzongs I ever came across. It is considered to be the second largest dzong in Bhutan which is located between thePho Chhu(Male) andMo Chhu(Female) river in the Punakha–valley. Almost all cities in Bhutan have at least two or three dzongs. But, none of them would match the beauty of this. Consider taking the best pictures of the dzong alongside the river view. We left to visit Suspension Bridge after having the maggie in the small petty shop opposite to the Dzong. Suspension Bridge, Punakha It is one of the oldest and second biggest bridges in Bhutan. It is located high above the Po Chhu river that spans about 180 meters in length. This iron chain bridge, in fact, seems scary for few but must consider walking along the bridge from one end to another. There is a small hotel on the opposite side which serves the best Tea along with biscuits. It was still 4 PM, so we had planned to travel Paro on the same day rather than halting. We started our journey towards Paro witnessing the amazing hill views. While we were traveling towards Paro, we had taken a slightly different route from which we came in the morning. It had a good long stretch of plain roads along the slight mountain curves. But nonetheless, seemed like a landslide zone where we could see a lot of boulders on the roads. We reached Paro around 6 PM and headed to our cottage which was situated in some village near to Paro. “Let’s have a drink today”, Amith said in excitement having seen the ambiance
“We’ll order some local drink as it is quite famous here”, I said calling out the girl to take the order.
“No, I will just have a beer and you have whatever local drink you want”, He added. We ordered a few beers and a big bottle of local drink which they usually serve it Tequilla glass. The entire big bottle costs just 120/-. It was so awesome that we bought one more bottle of the drink to sip during the trek. It was a great feeling for us with the typical village ambiance and wooden huts with a spongy mattress gave us a night of cozy sleep. We got up early in the morning and left for the trek having a complimentary Parota and the local drink which we had bought in the previous night. None of them drank except me and Sudheer. Tiger Nest, Paro We reached the foothill of the tiger nest and gazed the view up to the nest. My god!!!!!! I could see some tiny building situated on the sides of some mountain. It seemed like a huge building pasted on to the mountain wall. After the inquiry, we figured out that it is trek with the one side distance of 4.5 km. We had to travel three consecutive mountains to reach up there. Since Sudheer had come solo, he had to leave back due to climate conditions in North India. He didn’t want to risk on his way back home. We all three started to trek. It was almost an hour later we were really tired. Not able to put a single step further. Still, we had to make it. Initially, I took a lead and just went ahead grabbing a water bottle at the cafe in between. Apart from that cafe, we would get nothing even at the top of the hill or inside the tiger nest. “Aye, careful, watch your step”, She said as I skidded.
“Hey, thanks”, I replied making a gesture
“Not able to trek?”, she asked
“Oh no, these shoes are of riding ones. They have a bad grip to this terrain”, I replied
“I will go in front of you then, catch my hands if you skid again”, saying so she stretched her hands across so that I could hold them. While I continued, found a spectacular view with one heartbreaking scene. I was able to see the tiger nest but to reach there, I just have to cross one last mountain which is connected by 700 steps with a small waterfall in between. Imagine you have come all the way for about 4 km and then you see 700 steps to steep down and climb again to reach the nest. I did finish the trek before the other two and was making a conversation with Bengaluru team out there. Then got to know that in order to make an entry inside, we have to buy the tickets at the foothill. I was like WTF, why did not someone inform me or rather put up some board saying “Ticket Counter” at the foothill. My bad, I just sat making some conversation with one uncle there. He asked me would I be needing any help in talking to the security personnel to let me in by paying the same entrance fee to them. As said, I was totally done with all the monasteries and other Buddhists religious places during my Leh trip. I later asked them if he could arrange two tickets for my friends at least. He did great help talking to security personnel to let us in. I paid to the security to let Sachin and Amith in once they reach the top. But, one old couple where I had spoken to them while trekking came and offered me a free ticket as one person from their group could not trek and went back to the foothill. I waited for some more time for Sachin and Amith to come. We all went in and it was indeed a great one. We were shit tired since we had nothing except that one complimentary Parota which we had it in the morning. Tiger Nest got its name from the story that some Tibetan Guru had come to this place on sitting the tigress. Not sure with the exact story though. But from the top there, you would get an amazing view of huge mighty mountains. We made our way back to the foothill faster than we could even imagine. We slid all the way due to our improper trekking gears. 
Guess what? I met that girl again. The one who offered me the help when I skidded. We spoke quite for some time exchanging our names when we were getting down.
“Riya, you’re beautiful and I couldn’t resist admiring it”. I complimented her
she laughed and said, “Thank you and?”
“Alright then, it was fun talking to you. Take care”, I said stretching my hands
“You too, keep up the good smile, Bye”, she said shaking my hands for the one last time. We left the place after having some coffee and snacks in the nearby hotel, but we had not made any booking for accommodation for that day since we had planned to depart to Paro. We were very much strained and had to halt there unexpectedly. Neither of our phones had enough charge to book the rooms online. I parked my vehicle and started enquiring the hotels. It was at one hotel where Bengaluru boys, a team of 8 who had come in their bikes helped me to book the rooms. We had met a couple of times before in Pheuntsholing and in Thimpu. Cha Le La, Haa We had freshened up and left Paro to continue traveling towardsHaa Valley. It is one of the best valleys in Bhutan. But we couldn’t make it due to weather conditions. We drove around 35 km towards Haa to witness mesmerizing Cha Le La Pass. Cha le la,the highest motorable pass in Bhutan. This was the second place that gave me goosebumps after the Khardungla, Leh. I could still remember the beautiful sceneries en route. The lush green trees along the pinpoint curves with my GoPro capturing the ride was amazing. While we were getting back, Sachin’s bike ran out of fuel. Amith is out of our sight speeding his ride. I toed for a very small distance and since we were getting down the hill, we were able to reach the foothill. Luckily, the fuel station was at a one-kilometer distance. We somehow managed to get his vehicle there. We fueled our vehicles and started our journey back to Phuentsholing. We still had to ride for another 127 km. It started to drizzle, we were in no mood to stop as it may get worse and we would be struck right there. Also, we had nothing to stop by in between. We had no alternative than to choose going back to Paro or to wait there till drizzling stops. I had no interest in making a way back. It was still drizzling and I started the ride thinking nothing would happen. Sachin and Amith continued along. We got drenched in rain, experienced the heavy fog for some time as well. Yes, we managed to reach safely. The journey back to Phuentsoling was indeed challenging. Phuentsholing, Bhutan — Siliguri, India It was one last day for us and we had decided to head back to India.
We all bought some souvenirs and visited the crocodile park in Phentsholing. It was 11 AM when we started our journey back to Siliguri and reached there by 6 PM.
We handed over the keys bidding adios the REs. Since we had enough time to catch our flights, we visited Siliguri National Park which is really a not worthy place. Unfortunately, we had missed our flight though we had reached the airport at 4:30 PM for the 6:15 PM flight. It was rescheduled to 4 PM and I had got no information regarding the same. The officials informed me that I would have got a mail and a message which I failed to check. Thank god, both of which were not received and after making the complaint to the higher officer at the airport, we got seats in another flight for the same time. We reached Bengaluru around 1 AM with 4 hours layover in Delhi. “Bye guys, Cheers to one hell of a trip”, we cheered and left taking the bus. Itinerary Bengaluru > Siliguri > Phuentsholing > Thimpu > Punakha > Paro > Cha le la > Phuentsholing > Siliguri > Delhi > Bengaluru. Must Visit Tiger nest, Cha le la pass, Punakha. Cha le la and Punakha will not be covered by any package tours since it involves extra permits and other headaches Special Thanks Sachin Madan(co-traveler), proprietor of KC, Chikkaballapur Amith Vinayak(co-traveler), Risk analyst in Amazon, Bengaluru Sudheer(co-traveler), UX Developer, Bengaluru Santanu Banerjee, proprietor of Destination adventureshttp://destinationadventure.in/, Siliguri Namma Bengaluru boys, whom we met in Thimpu Riya, Pranic healer, Delhi To the old couple who offered me a free ticket to Tiger Nest Thanks for reading. 
Have a great day :)

We spoke quite for some time exchanging our names when we were getting down.
“Riya, you’re beautiful and I couldn’t resist admiring it”. I complimented her
she laughed and said, “Thank you and?”
“Alright then, it was fun talking to you. Take care”, I said stretching my hands
“You too, keep up the good smile, Bye”, she said shaking my hands for the one last time.

We left the place after having some coffee and snacks in the nearby hotel, but we had not made any booking for accommodation for that day since we had planned to depart to Paro. We were very much strained and had to halt there unexpectedly. Neither of our phones had enough charge to book the rooms online. I parked my vehicle and started enquiring the hotels. It was at one hotel where Bengaluru boys, a team of 8 who had come in their bikes helped me to book the rooms. We had met a couple of times before in Pheuntsholing and in Thimpu.
Cha Le La, Haa
We had freshened up and left Paro to continue traveling towards
Haa Valley
. It is one of the best valleys in Bhutan. But we couldn’t make it due to weather conditions. We drove around 35 km towards Haa to witness mesmerizing Cha Le La Pass.
Cha le la,
the highest motorable pass in Bhutan. This was the second place that gave me goosebumps after the Khardungla, Leh. I could still remember the beautiful sceneries en route.
The lush green trees along the pinpoint curves with my GoPro capturing the ride was amazing.

While we were getting back, Sachin’s bike ran out of fuel. Amith is out of our sight speeding his ride. I toed for a very small distance and since we were getting down the hill, we were able to reach the foothill. Luckily, the fuel station was at a one-kilometer distance. We somehow managed to get his vehicle there. We fueled our vehicles and started our journey back to Phuentsholing. We still had to ride for another 127 km.

It started to drizzle, we were in no mood to stop as it may get worse and we would be struck right there. Also, we had nothing to stop by in between. We had no alternative than to choose going back to Paro or to wait there till drizzling stops. I had no interest in making a way back. It was still drizzling and I started the ride thinking nothing would happen. Sachin and Amith continued along. We got drenched in rain, experienced the heavy fog for some time as well.
Yes, we managed to reach safely. The journey back to Phuentsoling was indeed challenging.
Phuentsholing, Bhutan — Siliguri, India
It was one last day for us and we had decided to head back to India.
We all bought some souvenirs and visited the crocodile park in Phentsholing. It was 11 AM when we started our journey back to Siliguri and reached there by 6 PM.
We handed over the keys bidding adios the REs.
Since we had enough time to catch our flights, we visited Siliguri National Park which is really a not worthy place.

Unfortunately, we had missed our flight though we had reached the airport at 4:30 PM for the 6:15 PM flight. It was rescheduled to 4 PM and I had got no information regarding the same. The officials informed me that I would have got a mail and a message which I failed to check. Thank god, both of which were not received and after making the complaint to the higher officer at the airport, we got seats in another flight for the same time.
We reached Bengaluru around 1 AM with 4 hours layover in Delhi.
“Bye guys, Cheers to one hell of a trip”, we cheered and left taking the bus.
Itinerary
Bengaluru > Siliguri > Phuentsholing > Thimpu > Punakha > Paro > Cha le la > Phuentsholing > Siliguri > Delhi > Bengaluru.
Must Visit
Tiger nest, Cha le la pass, Punakha.
Cha le la and Punakha will not be covered by any package tours since it involves extra permits and other headaches
